blocks.heading: A store manager asks: which product categories generate the most revenue?

items.question: Her options today
items.text: Wait about **three days** for an analyst, or **weeks** for a curated tool to be set up.
items.action: Or learn the schema and SQL herself.

items.question: What she needs
items.text: An answer **today**, the **SQL behind it** so she can check it, and her data **never changed**.
items.action: Other tools pay for meaning in setup; this project pays in **review**.

items.question: Why it is hard
items.text: Published scores fall from **91.2 %** on Spider 1.0 to **21.3 %** on enterprise tasks.
items.action: “Revenue” is not a column: meaning is the hard part.

items.question: Who else it serves
items.text: Managers new to a database, privacy-sensitive teams and teams with large schemas.
items.action: Not for metrics that must match across teams.

highlight: which product categories generate the most revenue?

blocks.heading: One question’s path: one model call, two gates in code
blocks.alt: Flowchart of the app in four stage lanes: prepare, generate, check and run, answer.
blocks.caption: Yellow is the model, teal is enforced in code. Only **79 of 608** stored values reach the model, never result rows; **45 of 45** read-only tests passed on 3 engines.

blocks.heading: The 21 % trap: why she needs the SQL
blocks.question: “Which product categories generate the most revenue?”
blocks.code_title: The SQL, and what “completed revenue” adds
blocks.caption: Electronics revenue, same top category. Neither is wrong: the SQL shows the choice, and **she decides**.

blocks.heading: Local 9B model: 64.6 % on Spider, 35.2 % on BIRD
blocks.caption: Answers matching the reference rows; this project’s scorer, not leaderboard scoring.

blocks.heading: On large databases, fewer tables scored higher
blocks.caption: 1,222 questions: **+3.6 [+1.4, +5.8]**, about 2 s slower. A dropped table cut top 6 to **5.4 %**; five later trials added no accuracy.

blocks.heading: What the store manager should know before she trusts it

items.question: Measured limits
items.text: About **one answer in three** did not match on Spider; **nothing checks meaning**.
items.action: A missed table usually means a wrong answer; table selection is about **2 s** slower.

items.question: Not yet tested
items.text: **Follow-up questions**, other languages, and **real company schemas** of hundreds of tables.
items.action: No user study yet, and running cost is not measured.

blocks.heading: About one answer in three is still wrong: four tests come before any default changes

items.question: New large schemas
items.text: The gain is from **2 of 4** databases.

blocks.text: **A first, checkable answer** for people who know the question but not the schema.
